first_impression.reaction: My daughter sent me this, so I read it properly. The opening is sensible and doesn't gush: 'March is a shoulder month for a wedding abroad, so the question is which kind of shoulder you want.' I like being told straight away that the islands are in cyclone season. I kept reading, but I was waiting the whole time for someone to mention deposits, contracts or who is responsible, and that only half comes, right at the end.

journey.quote: across much of the tropics the closing weeks of the wet or cyclone season, which is still that season.
journey.reaction: Good. Nobody's pretending Fiji in March is a sure thing. That honesty makes me trust the rest more.

journey.quote: Each station uses its own period and rain-day definition, so read every figure on its own and choose on trade-offs, not on numbers set side by side.
journey.reaction: I had to read this twice. I don't know what a rain-day definition is and I don't want to. Just tell me the figures are a rough guide.

journey.quote: Fiji, Mauritius and the Seychelles are inside the cyclone or monsoon season Smartraveller describes for March, so a covered ceremony option and a buffer day are part of the booking.
journey.reaction: Smartraveller I know and trust. A buffer day is a sensible, practical idea. My husband will like this.

journey.quote: How do guests who find steps or gravel paths hard reach the ceremony and the dining room?
journey.reaction: That's exactly my mother's walking frame question. I'm glad someone thought to ask it, and I'd ask it myself.

journey.quote: Milan's climate normals for 1971 to 2000, supplied by the Italian Air Force meteorological service, give a March mean daily minimum of 3.8°C, a mean daily maximum of 14.3°C and 65.0 mm of rain over 6.7 rain days.
journey.reaction: The 3.8 degrees is useful: Mum will need a proper coat and a heated room. But every entry has a paragraph like this, with station names and year ranges, and by the fifth one my eyes were glazing over on the iPad.

journey.quote: At a mean daily maximum above 31°C, older guests need shade, water and a cooler hour for the ceremony.
journey.reaction: Thank you. This is the sort of thing I worry about with my mother and my husband's aunt. It's practical and it's not patronising.

journey.quote: What happens to the wedding, and to guests' rooms, if a cyclone closes the airport that week?
journey.reaction: Right question. But the next one in my head is what happens to the money we've already paid, and the page never asks that.

journey.quote: What are the wet-weather and cyclone plans, and will you set them out in writing?
journey.reaction: 'In writing' is what I want to see. I'd like that kind of question for the deposit and the contract too, not just the weather plan.

journey.section: Shoulder season weather and a plan B
journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor confirms inclusions in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: Reassuring, but it's one short sentence tucked under a weather heading. It's the most important line on the page for me and it's easy to miss.

journey.quote: Ask each venue how older or less mobile guests move around in wet weather.
journey.reaction: Good, but it stops at getting around. If one of the older ones falls ill, how far are we from a doctor? That isn't mentioned anywhere.

journey.section: Plan your March wedding with Wedded Concierge
journey.quote: one Wedded Advisor, start to finish, works in your time zone and quotes in AUD, and the fee is agreed in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: This is what I was looking for: one person, Australian dollars, the fee in writing. Why is it only here at the very bottom? Half the people reading this won't get this far.

unanswered_questions: Is the money we pay a venue overseas protected if they cancel, or if a cyclone means the date has to move?
Who do I ring if something goes wrong at 2am their time? Is the Wedded Advisor reachable during the wedding week itself?
Can I speak to someone on the phone before anything is booked, or is it only an online form?
Are venue contracts in English, and are venue payments in AUD or the local currency?
Which travel insurance actually covers cyclone disruption and older guests with existing conditions? Who helps us check?
How far is medical help from these places if an older guest is unwell?

turn_offs_found.quote: Each station uses its own period and rain-day definition, so read every figure on its own and choose on trade-offs, not on numbers set side by side.
turn_offs_found.why: Technical and roundabout. It made me feel I was missing something. Plain words would do.

turn_offs_found.quote: On 25 and 26 March a deep subtropical low brought heavy rain and flooding, with states of emergency and road closures from Northland to the Bay of Plenty. As at November 2026, Smartraveller warns that weather can change quickly and that severe weather can leave travellers stranded, especially in remote areas.
turn_offs_found.why: Long, dense weather paragraphs, one after another. On an iPad they come out as a wall of text. Useful, but heavy going.

turn_offs_found.quote: Whether your March is a heated villa dinner on Lake Como or a pavilion ceremony in Fiji, one Wedded Advisor, start to finish, works in your time zone and quotes in AUD, and the fee is agreed in writing before any work begins.
turn_offs_found.why: Not a turn-off in itself. The problem is that the only real word about who is accountable and how the money works sits in the last paragraph. Everything above it is about the weather.

would_share_with: My husband, with a note asking about deposits and insurance
My daughter, back to her, with the Mauritius and Lake Como accessibility questions underlined

cta_reaction.quote: Tell us your date, your guest list and anyone who needs extra care getting there, and begin with Wedded Concierge.
cta_reaction.why: I like that it asks about anyone who needs extra care. That's my mother, and it tells me they've thought about her. But I want to speak to a person before I hand over details, and nothing here says I'll get a phone call. I'd likely leave it to my daughter to click and then ask her who rang.

top_3_changes: Give the venue questions a money-and-contract question, not just weather ones. NEW: "Ask each venue, in writing, what happens to your deposit if weather moves the date. Your Wedded Advisor confirms inclusions in writing before you commit."

Mention the Wedded Advisor and putting things in writing earlier, not only at the bottom. Edit (after the table) OLD: "Torn between a cool European spring and a warm, wet island? Talk it through with [Wedded Concierge](/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=wedding-destinations-march&utm_content=primary)." NEW: "Torn between a cool European spring and a warm, wet island? Talk it through with a Wedded Advisor at [Wedded Concierge](/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=wedding-destinations-march&utm_content=primary), who confirms inclusions in writing before you commit."

Put the weather-station caveat in plain words, and add a health question for older guests. Edit 1 (Key takeaways) OLD: "Each station uses its own period and rain-day definition, so read every figure on its own and choose on trade-offs, not on numbers set side by side." NEW: "The weather figures come from different stations and different years, so treat each one as a rough guide to that place, not as a way to compare places." Edit 2 (Guests travelling from Australia) OLD: "Ask each venue how older or less mobile guests move around in wet weather." NEW: "Ask each venue how older or less mobile guests move around in wet weather, and how far it is to the nearest doctor."

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off has an exact quote from the draft
Stayed in character as Margaret (funding parent, reading carefully on an iPad)
No invented brand facts; missing information listed in unanswered_questions
HTML comments, image slots and VERIFY markers treated as invisible
Suggested edits are exact old/new strings taken from the draft

Suggested edits add no prices, statistics, weather figures, 'best', rankings, 'free', vendor or venue names, fees, on-the-ground staff, transfers, room blocks, availability, holiday dates or legal claims

open_questions.question: The page never says whether a Wedded Advisor can be reached by phone, or during the wedding week. Can that be stated (with a source), or should it stay an open question for the CRO stage?
Deposit protection and contract language and currency for overseas venues are not covered. Is there sourced brand copy on this, or should the edit stay as a question for couples to ask the venue?
